A hardworking spell began when an early surprise was first spotted by the relief planner. Incident Report: Delay in Companion Animal Check-in Review

During the morning intake at Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk received notice that a pet crate had arrived without the usual matching release papers. The traveler was calm but concerned, and the pet, Milo, remained secure while the matter was examined. The desk agent alerted the senior coordinator, and the safety coordinator was asked to review the situation as a possible handling and documentation issue. The crate was kept in a designated holding area, away from other animals and traffic, so that the review could proceed without added stress.

The coordinator checked the travel file, the crate label, and the handover notes, then compared them with the booking record. <<FACT F118>> The review showed that the missing paperwork was related to an arrival transfer and not to a welfare concern. The traveler was advised to remain nearby while the desk confirmed the route history and notified the receiving team. No animal was moved until the file was reconciled and the crate could be tracked with confidence.

Handling steps were taken in order and with care. The desk updated the incident log, informed the ramp contact, and requested a second verification of the crate identity. The safety coordinator then confirmed that the crate seal remained intact and that the pet showed no sign of distress. Once the records matched, the traveler was given clear guidance on the next steps, including how the claim process would be handled if any item remained unaccounted for. The team also reminded staff to double-check transfer papers during future handoffs.

Follow-up will include a brief staff review, a reminder on document checks, and continued monitoring of any similar cases at Aurelia Skyways. The Companion Animal Travel Desk will keep the file open until all related records are resolved and confirmed. This matter was contained without injury, and the response met the expected standard of careful service.
